messages:
Raj: Quick follow-up from the all-hands  pricing & usage section. Two customer asks landed in my inbox: (1) can promo credits be restricted to non-production routes? (2) how do rate limits apply to multi-tenant demo keys?

Ava: Good questions. Promo credits are currently account-scoped currency only; they cannot be scoped to a route via the console today. We're evaluating tagged credits (route/org scoped) for enterprise in the roadmap.

Tomas: For demo/multi-tenant keys we enforce per-key QPS + per-route concurrency. If you share a demo key across many tenants, the shared key will hit limits faster. Recommend using per-tenant keys or per-route adapters with a gateway that does pooling. We log per-request key id so you can audit which tenants caused throttles.

Raj: Customers also want an easy example: "I have $500 in promo credits, I ran embeddings at peak  what's the expected behavior?"

Ava: Example blurb: "Promo credits reduce your payable balance; they do not raise throughput limits. If you have $500 promo, and you submit 10M tokens at $0.00005/token ($500), credits cover cost but requests may still be 429'd if you exceed RPS/concurrency. Check X-RateLimit-* headers and X-Credit-Balance."

Legal: Note on expiry: standard self-serve promo credits expire 12 months after issuance. Any custom enterprise promo can specify different terms in the contract. Also flag refunds/chargebacks: credits used are treated as consumed and cannot be refunded automatically; billing disputes handled case-by-case.

billing-bot: FYI: Console shows Credits balance at Console > Billing > Credits; API exposes X-Credit-Balance and Billing-Help link: https://console.redwood/billing/help/credits

Tomas: Ops nuance: we support a small onboarding burst pool for new signups (48h) to reduce churn. That pool is shared and finite; once exhausted, keys fall back to their per-key limits. For customers needing sustained high RPS, recommend Dedicated commit or request a temporary burst allocation via sales.

Raj: How about model fallback billing? If we automatically fallback to a lower-cost model during regional pressure, how is that billed and how will customers see it?

Ava: We bill for the model that actually served the request. We surface X-Model-Served and X-Fallback-Reason headers and list fallback events in Console > Routes > Activity. We'll add a per-request column in the billing export for clarity.

ops-bot: Pinned internal playbook: /handbook/ops/burst-and-rate-limit-playbook.md

Raj: One last: support wants a short sentence to paste when users say "I had credits but got 429"

Tomas: Paste-ready: "429 means your request rate exceeded the accounts configured throughput. Credits pay for token cost but do not increase request-rate capacity. Check X-RateLimit-* headers or request dedicated capacity if you need sustained higher throughput."

Ava: I'll add the FAQ snippet and a tiny example calc to the billing docs this week. Closing thread. :white_check_mark:
